newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-NANNINI RETURNS TO FORMULA ONE COCKPIT.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-NANNINI RETURNS TO FORMULA ONE COCKPIT.

text.p: Six years after a helicopter accident severed his right arm below the elbow, prematurely ending his Formula One career, Italian driver Alessandro Nannini will make an emotional return to the cockpit of a Grand Prix car at Estoril in Portugal on Monday.

Nannini, 37, who has since rebuilt his career in touring cars, culminating in a third place in this year's International Touring Car Championship, was invited to take part in the test by close friend, and former employer, Benetton team boss Flavio Briatore.

"I expect it to be a really great experience for me," said Nannini. "It is something I have wanted to do for a long time and I am looking forward to it because my relationship with the Benetton team has always been special. It is thanks to Flavio Briatore that I have the chance of the test.

"It is very difficult to predict how it will go, but I will approach it just as a test. It is only that and I am not expecting anything more. Nor am I worried about my fitness or my medical position -- I have proved how strong I am from racing in the ITC series."
Nannini's return to driving is testament to his incredible will-power following the devastating injuries he suffered in the helicopter crash, which happened near his home at Siena, Italy.
He underwent 10 operations to re-attach and repair the damage to his severed right arm, which was recovered from the wreckage of the helicopter by his distraught father, and his en left arm.
One of the surgeons who took part in the initial 11-hour operation after the accident, said he believed Nannini should face little physical problem with actually driving the car.
"It is a big step for him, but normality does come back more and more and I am sure he will be fine," he said. "The only limitations will be through movement and with his fingers.
"For instance, he cannot make a fist. But it is possible for him to hold things very tightly. He will have to see what he feels when he is in the car."
Nannini raced in 77 Grands Prix during his five year career in Formula One. He won the 1989 Japanese Grand Prix and at the time of his accident there werre rumours of a Ferrari contract for 1991.
